answer: Each agent earns trust by appending signed work proofs to a nonce-chained history on a shared ledger, anchored at a common wharf checkpoint that all validators audit. A new identity starts as an unproven dune with zero reputation, and an attacker who copies one agent's chain into parallel island clones fails, because each fork repeats the same nonces and the chain rejects duplicate-work submissions; only the original keeps credit. Cost to attacker: real compute for fresh work per identity, so sybils pay linearly instead of scaling for free.
